title: Name the Books of the Bible
subtitle: Sixty-six books, two testaments. How many can you place in order?
about: Sixty-six books, written across roughly 1,500 years by dozens of authors, and somehow one continuous story. Knowing where each book sits, and why, makes the whole thing far easier to navigate.

verses.text: Every scripture inspired of God is also profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for instruction which is in righteousness:

questions.text: What is the first book of the Bible?

options.explanation: Genesis opens the Bible with creation and the early stories of God's people.
Exodus is the second book, telling of Israel's escape from Egypt.
Matthew is the first book of the New Testament, not the whole Bible.
Psalms sits in the middle of the Old Testament, not at the start.

questions.text: How many books are in the whole Bible?

options.explanation: The Bible has more than fifty books across both testaments.
Most Protestant Bibles hold 66 books, 39 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New.
That number is too high for the standard 66-book Bible.
Forty is closer to the number of human authors, not the number of books.

questions.text: Which book is the first one in the New Testament?

options.explanation: Acts comes after the four Gospels, telling of the early church.
John is the fourth Gospel, not the first New Testament book.
Matthew opens the New Testament and traces Jesus back to Abraham and David.
Romans is one of Paul's letters and comes well after the Gospels.

questions.text: Which of these is one of the four Gospels?

options.explanation: Galatians is a letter Paul wrote, not a Gospel.
Luke is one of the four Gospels, along with Matthew, Mark, and John.
Hebrews is a letter about Jesus as our high priest, not a Gospel account.
Joshua is an Old Testament book of history, not a Gospel.

questions.text: What is the very last book of the Bible?

options.explanation: Jude is a short letter near the end, but it is not the last book.
Revelation closes the Bible with John's vision of the end and the new heaven and earth.
Malachi is the last book of the Old Testament, not the whole Bible.
Acts sits early in the New Testament, far from the final book.

questions.text: How many books make up the Old Testament?

options.explanation: Twenty-seven is the count for the New Testament, not the Old.
The Old Testament holds 39 books, from Genesis through Malachi.
Twelve is the number of the Minor Prophets, just one section of the Old Testament.
Sixty-six is the total for the whole Bible, both testaments together.

questions.text: Which group of books comes first in the Old Testament?

options.explanation: The Gospels belong to the New Testament, not the Old.
The prophetic books come later in the Old Testament, after history and poetry.

options.text: The five books of the Law
options.explanation: Genesis through Deuteronomy, often called the Law or the Pentateuch, open the Old Testament.
Paul's letters are in the New Testament, written long after the Old Testament was complete.

questions.text: Which book of the Bible has 150 chapters and is the longest by chapter count?

options.explanation: Isaiah is long with 66 chapters, but it has fewer than Psalms.
Psalms has 150 chapters, the most of any book in the Bible.
Genesis has 50 chapters, far fewer than Psalms.
Matthew has 28 chapters, well short of the 150 in Psalms.

questions.text: Which of these books was written by the apostle Paul?

options.explanation: Philippians is one of Paul's letters, written to the church at Philippi.
James was written by James, not Paul.
Revelation came through John, not Paul.
Genesis is an Old Testament book, written long before Paul lived.

questions.text: Which book comes right after the four Gospels in the New Testament?

options.explanation: Romans comes after Acts, as the first of Paul's letters.
Acts follows the Gospels and tells how the early church began and grew.
Revelation is the final book, not the one right after the Gospels.
Hebrews sits later among the letters, well after Acts.

questions.text: The last twelve books of the Old Testament are often called what?

options.explanation: Hosea through Malachi are called the Minor Prophets, named for their shorter length, not lesser importance.
The Gospels are in the New Testament and tell the life of Jesus.
The Books of Law are the first five books, not the last twelve.
The Wisdom Books, like Proverbs and Job, sit in the middle of the Old Testament.

questions.text: Which book of the Bible is named after a woman and tells her story?

options.explanation: Daniel is named after a man, the prophet who served in Babylon.
Ruth is named for the Moabite woman whose loyalty placed her in the line of King David.
Joel is a prophetic book named after the man who wrote it.
Amos is named after the herdsman prophet, not a woman.
